<text:style bold="true">Materials</text:style>

<image:base64 col="0" width="21" wrap="none"></image:base64>

Choosing Materials in the menu of the panel changes the nine buttons into nine
materials. They are used exactly like colours: the primary one (click) is for the
strokes, the secondary one (double click, Ctrl+click or the right button menu) for
the fills. The lines made of a material look like tubes, lit by the light and with
their reflections; the fills look like surfaces of that material. The look depends
on the light: see the Light of the layer button in the Artistic Tools. The buttons
of this panel are always active.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Gold</text:style>
Warm yellow metal, with a broad soft highlight and a deep amber shade.


<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Chrome</text:style>
Bright mirror-like metal: it reflects a light sky and a dark ground, with a
sharp horizon between them.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Copper</text:style>
Reddish metal, polished like the gold.


<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Magnesium alloy</text:style>
Satin gray metal with a fine brushing along one direction.


<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Metallic black</text:style>
A very dark glossy metal with tiny bright flakes and a strong highlight.


<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Teak wood</text:style>
Warm brown wood with the grain running along the line or the surface.


<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Glass</text:style>
Almost transparent: it becomes denser at the edges and has white highlights.


<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Marble</text:style>
Whitish polished stone with gray veins.


<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Granite</text:style>
Speckled stone, made of gray, black, white and pinkish grains.


Every material can be adjusted: a click with the right button on its button, then
"Change material...", opens a window with a sample (a bar, a plate and a sphere) and
the parameters. Roughness scatters the reflections (0 polished, 100 satin). Texture
step is the size of the grain, the veins or the flakes, and Texture direction the
way they run; Texture strength is how much the texture shows. Gloss is the strength
of the highlights, Brightness and Opacity are what they say, and Colour multiplies
the material by a colour (for instance a pinkish one for a rose gold). Reset all
gives the material back as it was made. All the objects made of that material follow
the change, and the changes are saved in the file.

The Glass has two more parameters. Thickness (0 to 100) is how thick the glass is: a
thicker glass absorbs more light, so it is greener, more opaque and has stronger edges.
Curve goes from concave (negative) to convex (positive), 0 is a flat sheet. A convex
glass is a magnifying lens: it enlarges what is seen through it, its highlight moves
to the other side and it is thicker in the middle; a concave one does the opposite and
shrinks what is behind it, and it is thicker at the edge. The more the glass is
thick, the more the curve bends the light. Curve centre X and Curve centre Y (0 to 100, 50 is the middle) move the centre of
the curve on the surface: the lens, its highlight and the thickest or thinnest point
are then around that point, as for a lens that is off centre. The sample shows the effect on the plate
(the squares behind it are enlarged or shrunk). With both at 0 the glass looks as it
always did. The curve shapes the fill of a surface; the stroke of a line (a tube) takes
only the thickness.
